pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Children of Joseph — the old father laying his hand on the boy's head while the family stands round the bed, for the choirmaster a maskil of the sons of Korah, we have heard with our ears O God
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jacob_blessing_the_children_of_joseph

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Portrait of the Artist's Mother — the old woman leaning on her staff in her hood and heavy cloak, our fathers have told us, the work You did in their days
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_portrait_of_the_artists_mother

pictures.scene: John Martin, Joshua Commanding the Sun to Stand Still — the captain with his arms stretched out over the valley while the armies fight under the storm, in the days of old, with Your hand You drove out the nations
pictures.name: pd_john_martin_joshua_commanding_the_sun_to_stand_still

pictures.scene: Jean-François Millet, The Angelus — the two on their own field standing still over the basket at the hour of prayer, and planted our fathers there, You crushed the peoples
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_angelus

pictures.scene: Paolo Veronese, Allegory of the Battle of Lepanto — the fleets locked together on the sea below while heaven is opened above them, and cast them out, for it was not by their sword that they took the land
pictures.name: pd_veronese_allegory_of_the_battle_of_lepanto

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, Victory O Lord! — Moses held up on the hill with his arms supported on either side, their arm did not bring them victory, it was by Your right hand
pictures.name: pd_millais_victory_o_lord

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, The Transfiguration — Christ standing with His arms spread wide in the white light on the mountain, Your arm and the light of Your face, because You favored them
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_the_transfiguration

pictures.scene: Hans Memling, Christ Blessing — the face of the Lord raised with His hand lifted over the book, You are my King O God, who ordains victories for Jacob
pictures.name: pd_memling_christ_blessing

pictures.scene: Albrecht Altdorfer, The Battle of Alexander at Issus — the whole plain filled with lances and standards under the burning sky, through You we repel our foes, through Your name we trample our enemies
pictures.name: pd_altdorfer_the_battle_of_alexander_at_issus

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, The Knights of Christ — the riders coming up in their armour behind the cross on their banner, for I do not trust in my bow, nor does my sword save me
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_the_knights_of_christ

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Belshazzar's Feast — the king turning from his table as the writing comes out on the wall of the hall, for You save us from our enemies, You put those who hate us to shame
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Tabernacle of the Linaioli — the Mother and the Child set in gold with the angels playing round the panel, in God we have boasted all day long, and Your name we will praise forever
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_tabernacle_of_the_linaioli

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jeremiah Lamenting the Destruction of Jerusalem — the prophet leaning his head on his hand in the dark while the city burns behind him, Selah, but You have rejected and humbled us
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jeremiah_lamenting_the_destruction_of_jerusalem

pictures.scene: Giotto, The Flight into Egypt — the family going out of the country with the donkey on the road under the rock, You no longer go forth with our armies, You have made us retreat from the foe
pictures.name: pd_giotto_the_flight_into_egypt

pictures.scene: David Roberts, The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem — the temple and the walls going up in smoke with the city taken, and those who hate us have plundered us, You have given us up as sheep to be devoured
pictures.name: pd_roberts_the_siege_and_destruction_of_jerusalem

pictures.scene: Eduard Bendemann, Jews Mourning in Exile — the captives sitting down together by the water in a strange country, You have scattered us among the nations, You sell Your people for nothing
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_jews_mourning_in_exile

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, Christ Crowned with Thorns — the Lord standing quiet in the middle while the four press in around Him, no profit do You gain from their sale, You have made us a reproach to our neighbors
pictures.name: pd_bosch_christ_crowned_with_thorns

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Netherlandish Proverbs — the village acting out all the old sayings at once in front of its houses, a mockery and derision to those around us, You have made us a byword among the nations
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_netherlandish_proverbs

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, The Mocking of Christ — the Lord seated blindfolded with the hands and faces of the mockers around Him, a laughingstock among the peoples, all day long my disgrace is before me
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_the_mocking_of_christ

pictures.scene: Hans Memling, Saint Veronica — the woman holding out the cloth with the face of the Lord printed on it, and shame has covered my face, at the voice of the scorner and reviler
pictures.name: pd_memling_saint_veronica

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Taking of Christ — the armed men closing their hands on Him in the lantern light, because of the enemy bent on revenge, all this has come upon us
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_taking_of_christ

pictures.scene: Leonardo da Vinci, The Last Supper — the Lord at the middle of the long table with the bread and the cup before Him, though we have not forgotten You, or betrayed Your covenant
pictures.name: pd_leonardo_the_last_supper

pictures.scene: Meindert Hobbema, The Avenue at Middelharnis — the straight road running away between the tall trees to the village, our hearts have not turned back, our steps have not strayed from Your path
pictures.name: pd_hobbema_the_avenue_at_middelharnis

pictures.scene: El Greco, The Agony in the Garden — the Lord kneeling alone on the rock in the night under the broken sky, but You have crushed us in the lair of jackals, You have covered us with deepest darkness
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_the_agony_in_the_garden

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching at Athens — the apostle standing up with his hands raised before the men of the city and their altars, if we had forgotten the name of our God, or spread out our hands to a foreign god
pictures.name: pd_raphael_st_paul_preaching_at_athens

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery — the woman kneeling in the light of the great temple while the accusers stand over her, would not God have discovered, since He knows the secrets of the heart
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_christ_and_the_woman_taken_in_adultery

pictures.scene: Francisco de Zurbarán, Agnus Dei — the lamb lying bound on the stone with its feet tied together, yet for Your sake we face death all day long, we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered
pictures.name: pd_zurbaran_agnus_dei

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee — the boat driven up on the wave with the sail tearing and the men crying out, wake up O Lord why are You sleeping, arise do not reject us forever
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_christ_in_the_storm_on_the_sea_of_galilee

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, Supper at Emmaus — the two at the table only now seeing who has broken the bread with them, why do You hide Your face, and forget our affliction and oppression
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_supper_at_emmaus

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Return of the Prodigal Son — the son down on his knees in his rags with the father's hands on his shoulders, for our soul has sunk to the dust, our bodies cling to the earth
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_return_of_the_prodigal_son

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Noli me tangere — the risen Lord in the garden turning to the woman kneeling by the empty tomb, rise up be our help, redeem us on account of Your loving devotion
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_noli_me_tangere

lines.text: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah.
We have heard with our ears, O God;
our fathers have told us
the work You did in their days,
in the days of old.
With Your hand You drove out the nations
and planted our fathers there;
You crushed the peoples
and cast them out.
For it was not by their sword that they took the land;
their arm did not bring them victory.
It was by Your right hand,
Your arm, and the light of Your face,
because You favored them.
You are my King, O God,
who ordains victories for Jacob.
Through You we repel our foes;
through Your name we trample our enemies.
For I do not trust in my bow,
nor does my sword save me.
For You save us from our enemies;
You put those who hate us to shame.
In God we have boasted all day long,
and Your name we will praise forever.
Selah
But You have rejected and humbled us;
You no longer go forth with our armies.
You have made us retreat from the foe,
and those who hate us have plundered us.
You have given us up as sheep to be devoured;
You have scattered us among the nations.
You sell Your people for nothing;
no profit do You gain from their sale.
You have made us a reproach to our neighbors,
a mockery and derision to those around us.
You have made us a byword among the nations,
a laughingstock among the peoples.
All day long my disgrace is before me,
and shame has covered my face,
at the voice of the scorner and reviler,
because of the enemy, bent on revenge.
All this has come upon us,
though we have not forgotten You
or betrayed Your covenant.
Our hearts have not turned back;
our steps have not strayed from Your path.
But You have crushed us in the lair of jackals;
You have covered us with deepest darkness.
If we had forgotten the name of our God
or spread out our hands to a foreign god,
would not God have discovered,
since He knows the secrets of the heart?
Yet for Your sake we face death all day long;
we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.
Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping?
Arise! Do not reject us forever.
Why do You hide Your face
and forget our affliction and oppression?
For our soul has sunk to the dust;
our bodies cling to the earth.
Rise up; be our help!
Redeem us on account of Your loving devotion.
